messages.content:
A regular hexagon with side length 4 is subdivided into a lattice of 96 equilateral triangles of side length 1. Let $S$ be the set of all vertices of this lattice. Compute the number of nondegenerate triangles with vertices in $S$ that contain the center of the hexagon strictly in their interior.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Let \(O\) be the center of the hexagon. Use lattice coordinates \((x,y)\) where a point is
\[
x\mathbf e_1+y\mathbf e_2,
\]
with \(\mathbf e_1,\mathbf e_2\) unit vectors making a \(60^\circ\) angle.  
The hexagon of side length \(4\) centered at \(O\) is
\[
S=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb Z^2: |x|\le 4,\ |y|\le 4,\ |x+y|\le 4\}.
\]
It has \(61\) vertices, including \(O\).

A counted triangle cannot use \(O\). Also, if two vertices lie on the same ray from \(O\), or on opposite rays, then \(O\) lies on the line of a side, so \(O\) is not strictly interior. Thus a valid triangle has its vertices on three distinct rays from \(O\), and those three ray-directions must not be contained in any closed semicircle. Conversely, if three distinct non-opposite ray-directions are not contained in any closed semicircle, then any choice of positive lattice points on those rays gives a triangle containing \(O\) strictly.

Now enumerate the rays from \(O\). In the half-open \(60^\circ\) sector from \(0^\circ\) to \(60^\circ\), the primitive direction vectors, in increasing angle, are
\[
(1,0),\ (3,1),\ (2,1),\ (1,1),\ (1,2),\ (1,3).
\]
The number of lattice points on each such ray is \(\left\lfloor \frac{4}{u+v}\right\rfloor\), giving weights
\[
4,\ 1,\ 1,\ 2,\ 1,\ 1.
\]
By \(60^\circ\)-rotational symmetry, the \(36\) directed rays in cyclic order have weights repeating
\[
p=(4,1,1,2,1,1).
\]

Index the \(36\) rays \(0,1,\dots,35\) in cyclic order. Since the configuration has \(180^\circ\) symmetry, ray \(i+18\) is opposite ray \(i\). A triple of rays contains \(O\) strictly exactly when its three cyclic index-gaps are all \(<18\).

For a fixed starting ray, let the two forward gaps be \(a,b\). The third gap is \(36-a-b\), so the conditions are
\[
1\le a,b\le 17,\qquad a+b\ge 19.
\]
Because the weights repeat with period \(6\), define for residues \(A,B\pmod 6\)
\[
F_{A,B}=\sum_{r=0}^5 p_r p_{r+A}p_{r+B}.
\]
A direct computation gives
\[
F=
\begin{array}{c|cccccc}
A\backslash B&0&1&2&3&4&5\\ \hline
0&24&28&28&52&28&28\\
1&28&28&18&24&24&18\\
2&28&18&28&24&18&24\\
3&52&24&24&52&24&24\\
4&28&24&18&24&28&18\\
5&28&18&24&24&18&28
\end{array}
\]

Let \(N_{A,B}\) be the number of ordered pairs \((a,b)\) with
\[
1\le a,b\le 17,\quad a+b\ge 19,\quad a\equiv A\pmod 6,\quad a+b\equiv B\pmod 6.
\]
Counting the residues of \(1,\dots,17\) gives
\[
N=
\begin{array}{c|cccccc}
A\backslash B&0&1&2&3&4&5\\ \hline
0&1&3&3&3&3&3\\
1&3&3&3&3&3&3\\
2&3&6&3&3&3&3\\
3&3&6&6&3&3&3\\
4&3&6&6&6&3&3\\
5&3&6&6&6&6&3
\end{array}
\]

Multiplying entrywise and summing,
\[
\sum_{A,B=0}^5 F_{A,B}N_{A,B}=3444.
\]
The ordered-start count over all \(36\) rays is \(6\cdot 3444\), and each valid triangle is counted \(3\) times, once from each vertex. Therefore the desired number is
\[
\frac{6\cdot 3444}{3}=6888.
\]

\[
\boxed{6888}
\]
